verdict.rationale: First-party docs call x402 an open standard for HTTP per-request payments. They say it is now developed under vendor-neutral Linux Foundation governance, with a 'v2' version label, and the protocol SDK is published openly on npm by the x402 Foundation. However, no evidence points to a readable, versioned specification document or confirms its licence, and only the hosted CDP facilitator (not the protocol) is shown as key-gated. Missing for 10: a citable published spec document with explicit version history, licence terms confirming implementation without any agreement, and independent confirmation that a third party built from the spec alone.

support.subject: As a developer, the commerce protocol this product speaks is published as an open, versioned specification I can read and implement without signing anything

citations.quote: x402 is an open standard for adding per-request payments to HTTP
x402 is now developed under open, vendor-neutral governance, so the payment layer stays interoperable and free of lock-in to any one provider.
The x402 v2 support table lists exact, upto, and batch-settlement
published by the x402 Foundation with SLSA provenance
